the development of a method which should be useful for the determination of the primary structure of proteins in solution, and which should be applicable to proteins of unknown structure, as well as proteins which are not amenable to X-ray crystallographic studies.

the sequential assignment of protein 1H resonances by nuclear Overhausers is a generally applicable method, which is not limited to the amide protons of the backbone.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distances between amides of neighbouring residues in a polypeptide chain are generally short and that the distance distribution is strongly dependent on the amino acid type.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the distances between protons in a polypeptide chain are not completely random, but are strongly dependent on the conformation of the chain and the nature of the amino acid residues involved.
